gobagitems.name: Drinking Water
gobagitems.description: At least 3 liters per person per day
gobagitems.whyImportant: Dehydration is life-threatening during disasters. Clean water may be unavailable for days.

gobagitems.name: Cash (Small Bills)
gobagitems.description: At least ₱2,000 in small denominations
gobagitems.whyImportant: ATMs and card readers may be down during power outages. Cash is essential for emergency purchases.

gobagitems.name: Fire Extinguisher (Small)
gobagitems.description: Compact ABC dry chemical fire extinguisher
gobagitems.whyImportant: Small fires can be extinguished before becoming catastrophic. Required for high fire-risk households.

gobagitems.name: Duct Tape
gobagitems.description: Heavy-duty duct tape (1 roll)
gobagitems.whyImportant: Can seal windows against storm, patch leaks, create splints, or secure damaged structures temporarily.

gobagitems.name: Rain Poncho / Waterproof Jacket
gobagitems.description: Lightweight waterproof rain gear
gobagitems.whyImportant: Staying dry during typhoons and floods is critical to prevent hypothermia and maintain body temperature.

gobagitems.name: Spare Phone Charger
gobagitems.description: Extra charging cable and adapter
gobagitems.whyImportant: Lost or broken chargers during evacuation leave you unable to communicate or access digital documents.

gobagitems.name: N95 Respirator Masks
gobagitems.description: Heavy-duty N95 masks (box of 10)
gobagitems.whyImportant: Critical for high-risk areas with fire, volcanic ash, or heavy particulate matter in the air.

gobagitems.name: Non-perishable Food
gobagitems.description: Canned goods, biscuits, energy bars (3-day supply)
gobagitems.whyImportant: Food supply chains break down during disasters. Ready-to-eat food ensures you have energy to evacuate safely.

gobagitems.name: Important Documents
gobagitems.description: Birth certificates, IDs, insurance, land titles in waterproof folder
gobagitems.whyImportant: Documents are needed for government assistance, insurance claims, and identity verification after disasters.

gobagitems.name: Fully Charged Power Bank
gobagitems.description: At least 10,000mAh power bank, fully charged before disaster
gobagitems.whyImportant: Keeping your phone charged means staying connected with family and accessing emergency alerts.

gobagitems.name: Personal Medications
gobagitems.description: 7-day supply of maintenance medicines
gobagitems.whyImportant: Medical facilities may be inaccessible. Running out of critical medications during a disaster can be fatal.

gobagitems.name: Change of Clothes (3 days)
gobagitems.description: Comfortable, weather-appropriate clothing per person
gobagitems.whyImportant: Wet clothes can cause hypothermia. Clean clothing prevents skin infections in evacuation centers.

gobagitems.name: Life Vest / Floatation Device
gobagitems.description: Personal floatation device or life jacket
gobagitems.whyImportant: Essential for flood-prone areas. Prevents drowning during flash floods or deep floodwater evacuation.

gobagitems.name: Manual Can Opener
gobagitems.description: Non-electric can opener for canned food
gobagitems.whyImportant: Useless to have canned food without a way to open it during power outages.

gobagitems.name: Alcohol / Hand Sanitizer
gobagitems.description: 70% isopropyl alcohol or hand sanitizer (250ml)
gobagitems.whyImportant: Prevents spread of disease when access to clean water for handwashing is limited.

gobagitems.name: First Aid Kit
gobagitems.description: Bandages, antiseptic, gauze, adhesive tape, scissors, gloves
gobagitems.whyImportant: Injuries are common during disasters. A first aid kit can prevent infections and save lives before medical help arrives.

gobagitems.name: Flashlight with Extra Batteries
gobagitems.description: LED flashlight with 2 sets of spare batteries
gobagitems.whyImportant: Power outages are common during disasters. Light is essential for safe navigation and signaling for help.

gobagitems.name: Rope (10 meters)
gobagitems.description: Strong nylon rope for climbing, securing items, or rescue
gobagitems.whyImportant: Useful for flood evacuation, securing go bag to body, or assisting others during rescue.

gobagitems.name: Blanket or Emergency Mylar Blanket
gobagitems.description: Thermal blanket for warmth
gobagitems.whyImportant: Evacuation centers can be cold. Mylar blankets are lightweight and retain 90% of body heat.

gobagitems.name: Face Masks
gobagitems.description: N95 or surgical masks (at least 5 per person)
gobagitems.whyImportant: Smoke, dust, and air-borne contaminants are common during disasters like fires and structural collapses.

gobagitems.name: Emergency Contact List
gobagitems.description: Written list of family, neighbors, MDRRMO, BFP contacts
gobagitems.whyImportant: Phone batteries die. A written contact list ensures you can reach help even without a charged phone.

gobagitems.name: Whistle
gobagitems.description: Loud safety whistle for signaling
gobagitems.whyImportant: If trapped under debris, a whistle can be heard much farther than your voice and uses less energy.

gobagitems.name: Waterproof Bag / Dry Bag
gobagitems.description: Large waterproof bag to protect go bag contents
gobagitems.whyImportant: Flood water can destroy documents and electronics. Waterproof protection preserves critical items.

gobagitems.name: Multi-tool or Swiss Army Knife
gobagitems.description: Compact multi-tool with knife, pliers, screwdriver
gobagitems.whyImportant: Versatile tool for cutting, prying, or repairing during emergencies when specialized tools aren't available.

gobagitems.name: Battery-powered or Hand-crank Radio
gobagitems.description: AM/FM radio for emergency broadcasts
gobagitems.whyImportant: Official updates from PAGASA, NDRRMC, and LGU are broadcast via radio when internet and TV are down.
